newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch call prices rise further, some see rate hike.
newsitem.headline: Dutch call prices rise further, some see rate hike.

text.p: Overnight guilders rose sharply in routine trade on Wednesday, with dealers citing a shortage of liquidity as the current seven-day special advances pact neared its close.
Call money closed the session at 3.25 percent after frequently trading as high as 3.50 percent. Despite the spikes higher, call money still ended near Tuesday's prices of 3.18-3.25 percent.
Dealers were split on whether the higher call rates would mean a short-term liquidity rate rise when the Dutch central bank sets a new special advances pact on Thursday.

"I don't think there's a real risk of a hike in interest rates," one said. "There has been a lot of upheaval about guilder weakness, but it never substantially breached its central rate (against the mark)."
But he conceded the market was debating about the chances of a special advances rate rise.
On Tuesday, the guilder was trading near its 112.673 exchange rate mechanism central rate against the mark.
Dealers said it started Wednesday around 112.70 but later recovered to 112.63 per 100 marks. "Some players have clearly been speculating on the mark/guilder cross," one said.
Longer-dated guilders also traded a touch higher on Wednesday, dealers said.
